{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693796101,"sessionID":"ses_e23ebc550ffeomauw9XOLPaGeH","part":{"id":"prt_1dc1608a70018C6LoNqAKNcAX6","messageID":"msg_1dc15e8fa00167FjXeUImOE0CY","sessionID":"ses_e23ebc550ffeomauw9XOLPaGeH","type":"text","text":"The shift is over. All four customer-facing services were at 0% errors from minute 48 to the end, apart from a fault in flags-svc that took mobile-api to about 68% errors from minute 57 to 74. One of my actions made things worse: rolling back payments-svc (a backend service) pushed web-storefront, the main revenue source, to 55–65% errors for about 10 minutes.\n\n**What was broken and what I did**\n\n1. **payments-svc bad deploy (web-storefront and partner-api at 4% errors).** Deploy v103 replaced a lookup that defaulted to EUR with one that crashes when `currency` is missing (\"KeyError: 'currency'\"). The errors passed up through fraud-svc and recommendations-svc to the customer-facing services. I rolled the deploy back.\n   - **My mistake:** payments-svc was already at 86% CPU. The requests that failed during the rollback were retried, which overloaded it, and it stayed overloaded after the rollback finished. Web-storefront rose to 55–65% errors from about minute 24 to 33.\n   - I cleared the overload by having payments-svc reject 65% of requests up front for 2 minutes (those rejections aren't retried), then removed the limit. Web-storefront went to 0% errors at minute 34.\n   - I should have limited incoming requests before starting the rollback.\n2. **media-store primary node gone (mobile-api and admin-portal at about 90% errors).** The logs showed \"primary node unreachable\". Failed requests were being retried until media-store was over capacity. I rejected 60% of its requests up front to break the retry loop, promoted the standby, then removed the limit.\n3. **address-svc traffic surge.** Its traffic rose from about 190 to over 500 requests per second around minute −9, with no recent changes, and it was dropping requests. I scaled it from 8 to 24 replicas. The scale-up landed at minute 47, CPU fell to 0.69, and mobile-api and admin-portal went to 0% errors.\n   - It stays at 24 replicas until the end of the shift, which costs about $48 a minute.\n4. **New fault at minute 57: flags-svc deploy v135 (\"query tuning\").** It caused connection-pool timeouts, and mobile-api errors rose to about 68%. The config change made at the same minute was harmless, so I rolled back the deploy instead. It finished at minute 74 and errors went to 0%.\n\n**Not causes:** recommendations-svc's high CPU came from its nightly-rollup job, and none of the other recent changes I checked were behind any errors.\n\n**Still in place:** No limits on incoming requests are left on. The only extra cost still running is the address-svc scale-up. Every mitigation went to a service that actually had a fault or was overloaded.","time":{"start":1794693793959,"end":1794693796097}}}
